review_protocol: score-blind AI-assisted qualitative review; single reviewer; not independent human evidence

ratings.reason: A four-mana 3/4 with repeat artifact drain is a strong speculative third pick in an artifact-rich set. Flagship already offers artifacts through cycling, but no black commitment; Quickwelder and Surveyor better preserve existing colors.
Cheap black artifact flyer with surveil fits both earlier black spells and supplies a crew body for the two Vehicles. Excellent curve and color fit; the green creature is also reasonable.

Efficient green three-drop with speed and late value fits a prospective BG deck with Broodwagon. Colorless Rover Blades keeps options open, but green is already represented and there is no comparably strong black spell.

White is supported only by an off-lane tapped land, and the UR-heavy pool has no Mount or Vehicle for the expensive activation. Camera Launcher and Walking Sarcophagus are flexible alternatives that fit the existing spells.

Basri's tokens and Veloheart Bike support the creature/Vehicle-count removal, and artifact destruction is useful in the format. Grim Bauble and Nesting Bot are also strong options; the early pool is still open.
Green is established, there are cheap creatures to deal damage, and two prior Dragons enable the surveil bonus. Efficient removal with good context; Sultai Monument is a credible fixing alternative.
Efficient green removal can reveal Whirlwing Stormbrood and complements its green Omen. The prior pick does not lock colors; Temur Devotee and Dispelling Exhale are also appealing.

The tri-land supplies green but not white despite two strong white spells already drafted, and no blue/red spells yet. Dragonback Lancer and Trade Route Envoy are useful established-color choices; speculative fixing is possible but mismatched.

Battlecrier is an efficient 4/3 with powerful discounts and works with Lasyd Prowler's power five. Three different colored pips are a real cost this early, so flexible Tawnyback and the green options remain competitive.

Cheap cantrip enables Cori-Steel Cutter's second-spell trigger, has late harmonize and can be recovered with Trawlers. Blue is established, although Bell-Ringer and Narset's Rebuke may be more impactful board interaction.

A black 2/8 is castable in the Abzan pool and has genuine high-toughness synergy with Kheru Bloodsucker. The pool already has expensive bodies; Sultai Banner can fix BG and accelerate, so Mastodon is a low-upside late choice.

Warden supports the red-white start with Jeskai as a realistic direction and can recover Arc Lightning for substantial value. The third color and five-mana cost make Wind-Scarred Crag and Alabaster Kirin serious competitors.

Feat is a strong single-white combat trick and early speculation is acceptable. The pool has a GU bomb and matching land, however, while Savage Punch is on-color efficient interaction with a potential ferocious enabler.

Secret Plans is a narrow GU morph engine with no face-down cards and no corresponding color support in Bloodstained Mire or Utter End. Feat of Resistance, Raiders' Spoils and Unyielding Krumar build toward existing colors.

Waterwhirl is a credible two-creature tempo swing in the slow format and Swiftwater Cliffs supports blue. Double blue at six mana is demanding with Crackling Doom and the five-color pull; Scaldkin, Throttle, Bloodfell Caves and other choices can better manage that risk.

Gandalf is a strong standalone removal-plus-body at six mana, and one previous gold pick does not establish a lane. Double red conflicts with Bard's Company, while Dwarven Shortsword, Harper and flexible Mirkwood Nurturer preserve more options.

Three mana for a drawn card and amass two is strong resource generation in established black, with a previous amass Saga and deathtouch Wolf. Troll Negotiations is attractive in green but requires an additional green commitment.

An efficient red two-drop that amasses repeatedly with noncreature spells supports RB, equipment casts and the Rampager's sacrifice plan. Strong on-color black alternatives such as Reverent Howl and Down to Goblin-town compete.

Dain supplies his own Axe and makes equipped attackers powerful, so there is a real standalone reason to branch at pick two. The first pick pulls GU, and flexible Mirkwood Nurturer or fixing is a safer fit; Dain's ceiling depends on equipment density.

A 3/2 trample Dwarf plus Treasure at three mana is efficient and directly fits the established RW Dwarf/equipment pool. Trample benefits from Dain's equipped-attacker double strike and the Treasure adds flexibility.

A resilient blue flying threat can generate meaningful value with noncreature spells, but the first pick is RG and the pack has strong acceleration, lands and archetype enablers. Blue speculation is reasonable at pick two but the synergy is not yet established.

Jadar is a low-cost repeatable token source that feeds Staff of the Storyteller, and Scrubland plus fast mana gives plausible access. The pool is RW-heavy; Revoker and Memory Jar offer powerful colorless alternatives.

A tapped RG manland has no current green spells or red creature plan, while the pool is blue/black artifact/combo leaning. Collective Brutality fits black and Currency Converter; Shelldock Isle is a much more plausible blue land.

Lens is a cheap body and potential card engine in a pool with white access, haste creatures and red threats. The existing pool is scattered and Phelia, Kellan and Bayou are especially attractive; Lens has no compelling dedicated synergy yet.

An eleven-mana green payoff has no credible cheat-into-play enabler in the drafted pool and its shuffle trigger is awkward for ordinary reanimation. Saheeli directly works with the red noncreature/artifact/token core, while Boots is flexible and cheap.
